text: Lesson 23 left four hypotheses on the table. This lesson confirms each one with real diagnostic evidence instead of a guess, and finds that three of them are genuinely contributing -- not just one.

The list view filters on store region and an active flag -- a condition every one of the 500 stores runs every morning. Its query plan shows a full table scan across 2.1 million rows to return a few hundred matches. No index exists on that store-region field. At 50 stores that scan was invisible. At 500, it's doing thousands of times more work than it needs to.

The approval flow calls a Script Include called ChecklistUtils. Reading its source turns up a classic query-in-a-loop: for every checklist item in an approval batch, it runs a brand-new GlideRecord query against the store config table. At 50 stores, batches were small enough that nobody noticed. At 500, a single batch can trigger dozens of redundant round trips.

The fix pulls that query outside the loop entirely, running it exactly once and building a lookup map that the loop simply reads from. Same inputs, same result, one query total instead of one query per item -- the exact query-in-a-loop fix this course covered earlier, confirmed here against a real symptom.

Two scheduled jobs -- a nightly rollup and a morning reminder -- have run for years against the same semaphore pool used for background transactions. At 50 stores that pool never saturated. At 500 stores, those two jobs plus the 7 AM submission spike saturate it completely, so every other transaction has to queue -- exactly the 40-minute, platform-wide slowdown that got this escalated.

All three causes were confirmed independently, with their own evidence, and fixing only one would leave real symptoms unexplained. Next, Lesson 25 applies all three fixes and builds the prevention plan that keeps this from happening again.
